questions.title: Integer-String Concatenator
questions.description:
Practice type conversion: read an integer and print a sentence that interpolates it as a string.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
One line: The number is <n>

Constraints:
-1000 <= n <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
puts "The number is #{n}"

questions.title: Float Truncator Drill
questions.description:
Practice converting a float string to an integer: read a decimal number as a string and print its integer (truncated) value.

Input Format:
A single line containing a float string (e.g. 3.99).

Output Format:
A single integer.

Constraints:
The string represents a finite number between -1000 and 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
puts s.to_i

questions.title: String Plus One Converter
questions.description:
Read a string that represents an integer and print that integer plus one.

Input Format:
A single line containing a string of digits (with optional leading minus sign).

Output Format:
A single integer: to_i(s) + 1.

Constraints:
-1000 <= parsed integer <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
puts s.to_i + 1

questions.title: String Class Reporter
questions.description:
Use Ruby's .class method to identify the type of an object. Read a string and print the name of its class.

Input Format:
A single line containing a string (no spaces).

Output Format:
One line: the class name (e.g. String).

Constraints:
1 <= string length <= 50.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
puts s.class

questions.title: Integer Class Reporter
questions.description:
Read an integer and print the name of its Ruby class.

Input Format:
A single integer on one line.

Output Format:
One line: the class name (e.g. Integer).

Constraints:
-10^9 <= n <= 10^9.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
puts n.class

questions.title: Symbol Identity Check
questions.description:
Read two strings and check whether their symbol conversions are equal. Print "same" or "different".

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated strings a and b.

Output Format:
One line: same or different.

Constraints:
1 <= length of each string <= 30.
questions.sourcecode:
a, b = gets.split
puts a.to_sym == b.to_sym ? "same" : "different"

questions.title: Bill Split Calculator
questions.description:
Three friends split a restaurant bill. Read total amount and number of people, then print each person's share to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers: total rupees, number of people.

Output Format:
One line: per-person share to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= total <= 10^6, 1 <= people <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
total, people = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
per_person = total.to_f / people
puts "%.2f" % per_person

questions.title: Fahrenheit to Celsius Converter
questions.description:
A weather app converts Fahrenheit (integer input) to Celsius using the formula C = (F - 32) * 5 / 9. Output the result to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
A single integer: temperature in Fahrenheit.

Output Format:
One line: Celsius value to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
-100 <= F <= 200.
questions.sourcecode:
f = gets.to_i
c = (f - 32) * 5.0 / 9
puts "%.2f" % c

questions.title: Score Percentage Reporter
questions.description:
A teacher's grading tool reads obtained and total marks (both integers) and prints the percentage to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers: obtained, total.

Output Format:
One line: percentage to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= obtained <= total <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
obtained, total = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
pct = obtained.to_f / total * 100
puts "%.2f" % pct

questions.title: Currency Rounder
questions.description:
A payment gateway reads a raw float string (rupees) and prints the amount rounded to 2 decimal places.

Input Format:
A single line containing a float string.

Output Format:
One line: the value to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= value <= 10^9.
questions.sourcecode:
x = gets.to_f
puts "%.2f" % x

questions.title: Sensor Reading Aggregator
questions.description:
A weather station collects n float temperature readings. Compute the average using a while loop (the builtin iterators are disabled). Print the average to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
First line: integer n. Following n lines: one float per line.

Output Format:
One line: average temperature to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, each reading between -100 and 200.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
total = 0.0
i = 0
while i < n
  total += gets.to_f
  i += 1
end
avg = total / n
puts "%.2f" % avg

questions.title: Numeric Class Identifier
questions.description:
A REPL tutor inspects a user-provided token and classifies it as Integer, Float, or String (without using the .class / is_a? family). Decide based on the token's characters.

Input Format:
A single line containing a token (no spaces).

Output Format:
One line: Integer, Float, or String.
  Integer: token is all digits with optional leading minus.
  Float: token contains a dot and digits around it (e.g. 3.14).
  String: otherwise.

Constraints:
1 <= token length <= 50.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
if s.include?(".")
  puts "Float"
elsif s.to_i.to_s == s
  puts "Integer"
else
  puts "String"
end

questions.title: Comment Stripper
questions.description:
A tiny Ruby preprocessor reads one line of Ruby source and removes any inline comment (the # character and everything after it). The slice/gsub/sub helpers are disabled; use split and include?.

Input Format:
A single line of Ruby source code (may or may not contain #).

Output Format:
One line: the source code with # and everything after removed (trailing whitespace is ignored by the judge).

Constraints:
1 <= line length <= 200.
questions.sourcecode:
line = gets.chomp
if line.include?("#")
  puts line.split("#")[0]
else
  puts line
end

questions.title: Guest Greeter with Empty Fallback
questions.description:
A chatbot greets a user by name. If the name is empty (or whitespace-only), it falls back to "Guest". Use the empty? check — the || and if/unless constructs are disabled to force the empty? approach.

Input Format:
A single line containing the visitor's name (may be empty or whitespace).

Output Format:
One line: Hello, <name>! or Hello, Guest!

Constraints:
0 <= name length <= 30.
questions.sourcecode:
name = gets.chomp.strip
name = name.empty? ? "Guest" : name
puts "Hello, #{name}!"

questions.title: Stock Ticker Multi-Parser
questions.description:
A fintech CLI tool reads a stock ticker record (symbol, integer share count, float price) and reports three values about it. The .class introspection methods are disabled.

Input Format:
A single line with 3 space-separated tokens: symbol shares price.

Output Format:
Three lines: symbol character count, integer share count, total value (shares * price) to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= symbol length <= 10, 1 <= shares <= 10^6, 0 <= price <= 10^6.
questions.sourcecode:
symbol, shares, price = gets.split
sym_len = symbol.length
n = shares.to_i
p = price.to_f
total = n * p
puts sym_len
puts n
puts "%.2f" % total

questions.title: Currency Exchange Reporter
questions.description:
A traveler enters an amount and an exchange rate (both as strings that may be integer or float). The script computes the converted amount to 2 decimals using to_f and split. Higher-order iterators are disabled.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated strings: amount, rate.

Output Format:
One line: converted amount (amount * rate) to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= amount, rate <= 10^6.
questions.sourcecode:
amount, rate = gets.split
a = amount.to_f
r = rate.to_f
result = a * r
puts "%.2f" % result

questions.title: Account Ledger Transfer
questions.description:
A bank ledger tool processes n transactions. Each transaction line is either "deposit <amount>" or "withdraw <amount>" where amount is a float string. Starting balance is 0.0. Print the final balance to 2 decimals using a while loop (iterators and sum are disabled).

Input Format:
First line: integer n. Following n lines: "deposit X" or "withdraw X".

Output Format:
One line: final balance to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= amount <= 10^6.
questions.blacklist: each, inject, reduce, sum, map, select
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
balance = 0.0
i = 0
while i < n
  op, amt = gets.split
  amount = amt.to_f
  if op == "deposit"
    balance += amount
  else
    balance -= amount
  end
  i += 1
end
puts "%.2f" % balance

questions.title: Inventory Value Calculator
questions.description:
A warehouse tool reads n inventory items, each line: name qty price (qty integer, price float). Compute total inventory value (sum of qty * price) and the number of bulk items (qty > 10). Higher-order iterators are disabled.

Input Format:
First line: integer n. Following n lines: name qty price (space-separated).

Output Format:
Two lines: total value to 2 decimals, then the count of bulk items.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= name length <= 20, 1 <= qty <= 10000, 0 <= price <= 10^6.
questions.blacklist: each, inject, reduce, sum, map, select
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
total_value = 0.0
bulk_items = 0
i = 0
while i < n
  name, qty, price = gets.split
  q = qty.to_i
  p = price.to_f
  total_value += q * p
  if q > 10
    bulk_items += 1
  end
  i += 1
end
puts "%.2f" % total_value
puts bulk_items

questions.title: Variable Type Inventory
questions.description:
A data logger records n lines, each tagged with a type label (int, float, or str) followed by a value. Count how many of each type appear. The case/when statement and higher-order iterators are disabled; use if/elsif and a while loop.

Input Format:
First line: integer n. Following n lines: "<type> <value>" where value may contain spaces (split on the first space only).

Output Format:
Three lines: count of int, count of float, count of str.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, type is one of int / float / str.
questions.sampleinput1:
5
int 42
float 3.14
str hello world
int 7
str foo
questions.input1:
4
float 1.5
float 2.5
str bar baz
int 9
questions.input3:
6
int 1
float 2.0
str x y z
int 4
float 5.5
str a b
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 1000, type is int / float / str
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
int_count = 0
float_count = 0
str_count = 0
i = 0
while i < n
  parts = gets.split(" ", 2)
  type = parts[0]
  if type == "int"
    int_count += 1
  elsif type == "float"
    float_count += 1
  elsif type == "str"
    str_count += 1
  end
  i += 1
end
puts int_count
puts float_count
puts str_count

questions.title: Multi-Category Field Aggregator
questions.description:
A personal-finance tool reads n ledger entries, each line: "<category> <amount>" where category is income, expense, or tax and amount is a float string. Aggregate totals per category. The case/when statement and higher-order iterators are disabled.

Input Format:
First line: integer n. Following n lines: "<category> <amount>".

Output Format:
Three lines: total income, total expense, total tax (each to 2 decimals).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= amount <= 10^6.
questions.input3:
6
income 1
income 2
expense 1
expense 2
tax 1
tax 2
questions.blacklist: case, when, each, inject, reduce, sum
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
income = 0.0
expense = 0.0
tax = 0.0
i = 0
while i < n
  cat, val = gets.split
  v = val.to_f
  if cat == "income"
    income += v
  elsif cat == "expense"
    expense += v
  elsif cat == "tax"
    tax += v
  end
  i += 1
end
puts "%.2f" % income
puts "%.2f" % expense
puts "%.2f" % tax
